newsitem.title: USA: AlliedSignal says earnings up 16 pct; splits stock.
newsitem.headline: AlliedSignal says earnings up 16 pct; splits stock.

text.p: AlliedSignal Inc. Wednesday reported a 16 percent jump in second-quarter earnings and announced a two-for-one stock split.
It earned $305 million, or $1.08 a share, vs. year-earlier earnings of $263 million, or 93 cents a share.
The aerospace and automotive products maker said sales rose 7 percent to $3.57 billion from $3.34 billion.
AlliedSignal's stock was up 62.5 cents at $91.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The company said its board of directors approved a two-for-one stock split and a regular quarterly dividend of 26 cents a share on the pre-split shares.
The dividend, which is unchanged from June's payment, is payable Sept. 10. for shareholders of record Aug. 21. The stock split is payable Sept. 15.
The company said the stock split was designed to make its stock price more attractive for individual investors. Since the last two-for-one stock split in March 1994, its stock has more than doubled.
AlliedSignal said sales increased 10 percent at its Aerospace unit and rose 7 percent in Engineered Materials, while edging up 2 percent at its Automotive division.
It said that in the second quarter, it completed or announced acquisitions that would boost its annual sales by $550 million.
